title: Identity provider migration
summary: Moving workforce authentication and provisioning between identity providers (for example Entra ID to Okta, or Okta to Entra ID). The directory, the apps, and the devices all depend on it, so the inventory of connections is the plan.

saml_sso.label: SAML SSO app
checks: NameID format and attribute mapping preserved per app (UPN vs email breaks account linking)
Vendor supports swapping IdP metadata, entity ID, and signing certificate
Test login with pilot users before flipping

oidc_sso.label: OIDC / OAuth SSO app
checks: Client ID/secret and redirect URIs re-registered in target
Claims and scopes mapped (groups, email, sub identifier stays stable)
Token lifetime and refresh behavior compared

scim_provisioning.label: SCIM / automated provisioning
checks: Import and match existing app accounts BEFORE enabling push to avoid duplicates or mass deactivation
Only one system may provision an app at a time: schedule the handoff
Attribute and role mapping verified on a test user

m365_federation.label: Microsoft 365 / domain federation
checks: Entra tenant remains the Microsoft 365 directory; scope is the authentication handoff, not deletion
Federation flip affects whole domains: use a staged approach or test domain
Hybrid join, Seamless SSO, and mail client modern auth tested

conditional_access.label: Conditional access / auth policy
checks: Each policy exported and mapped to a target authentication policy, with gaps listed
Named locations, risk signals, and device conditions reproduced or consciously dropped
Report-only or audit mode before enforcement

mfa_authenticators.label: MFA factors and passkeys
checks: Factors cannot be exported: plan re-enrollment campaign and helpdesk surge
FIDO2 keys and passkeys re-registered
Enrollment grace period and recovery path defined

device_trust.label: Device trust / compliance signal
checks: Compliance signal source (MDM) connected to the target IdP
Unmanaged device behavior decided
Hybrid-joined or Entra-joined Windows login behavior left unchanged in early waves

service_principal_api.label: Service principal / API / M2M auth
checks: Owner identified for each app registration or service account
Secrets and certificates rotated into target, expiry dates recorded
Graph or directory API consumers re-pointed

legacy_auth.label: Legacy / header-based / LDAP / RADIUS
checks: Decide replace, proxy (access gateway), or retire
LDAP/RADIUS interface stood up in target and tested
Network path and shared secrets re-issued

privileged_admin.label: Admin / privileged access
checks: Break-glass accounts remain outside the new IdP dependency
Admin role assignments reviewed, not copied blindly
Approval and PIM-style workflows replaced or documented

guest_b2b.label: Guest / external identities
checks: External user population counted and owners assigned
Invitation and trust model decided
Partner apps that trust the old tenant notified

group_directory.label: Groups / directory sync
checks: Nested and dynamic groups flattened or rebuilt as rules
Source of truth for groups decided (HRIS, directory, or IdP)
Group-based license and app assignment mapped

gotchas.title: Passwords cannot be exported
gotchas.detail: Hashes do not move between IdPs. Plan delegated authentication against on-prem AD, a staged password reset, or passwordless enrollment before the cutover, and budget helpdesk volume for it.

gotchas.title: Two provisioners fighting over one app
gotchas.detail: If both IdPs push SCIM to the same app, one can deprovision accounts the other just created. Hand off one app at a time and import-match first.

gotchas.title: The old tenant does not disappear
gotchas.detail: Organizations on Microsoft 365 keep the Entra tenant as the Microsoft directory. The project replaces the primary authentication and app-access layer, and the scope must say so to avoid a false decommission date.

gotchas.title: Group nesting and dynamic rules do not port
gotchas.detail: Target group models may be flat. Nested membership that granted app access silently stops working after migration.

gotchas.title: New single point of failure
gotchas.detail: Everything now authenticates through one vendor. Keep break-glass admin paths that do not depend on the new IdP and document the outage runbook.

gotchas.title: Audit trail discontinuity
gotchas.detail: Sign-in logs live in two places during transition. Keep old logs for the retention period and route the new ones to the SIEM before first cutover; SOC 2 evidence spans both.

gotchas.title: Verify vendor behavior
gotchas.detail: Feature gaps and limits change by release. Confirm each Critical and High item against current vendor documentation before committing dates.

entra>okta.title: NameID default differs
entra>okta.detail: Entra commonly emits UPN while Okta defaults to email. Apps keyed on the old value create duplicate users or lock people out. Record the format per app.

entra>okta.title: Conditional Access has no 1:1 export
entra>okta.detail: Policies must be re-expressed as Okta authentication policies and Device Assurance rules. Inventory every policy and list what is dropped.

entra>okta.title: Windows sign-in and join state
entra>okta.detail: Entra-joined or hybrid-joined devices keep their join. Replacing Windows login with an Okta device-access product is a separate decision, so defer it from the first waves.

entra>okta.title: App registrations used by automation
entra>okta.detail: Graph API consumers, scripts, and CI pipelines use Entra app registrations that have no Okta equivalent and break silently.

okta>entra.title: Okta groups and rules to Entra dynamic groups
okta>entra.detail: Okta group rules and app assignments map to Entra groups and enterprise app assignments with different evaluation behavior and licensing needs.

okta>entra.title: Okta Workflows and inline hooks
okta>entra.detail: Automations built in Okta Workflows or hooks have no direct Entra counterpart and must be rebuilt (Logic Apps, Power Automate, or custom).

okta>entra.title: Entra license tier gates features
okta>entra.detail: Conditional Access, PIM, and some provisioning features depend on license tier. Confirm licensing before the design is final.

discovery: Entra: export Enterprise Applications and App Registrations (portal CSV or Graph) with SSO type, assigned users, and last sign-in
Entra: pull 90 days of sign-in logs by application to find real usage and dead apps
Entra: export all Conditional Access policies, named locations, and authentication methods policy
Okta: export Applications, Groups, Group Rules, Policies, and System Log activity by app
Ask app owners and Finance (SaaS spend list) for apps that never touched the IdP
Search code and CI for client secrets, tenant IDs, and issuer URLs

phases.name: Discover and decide
activities: Retire dead apps before migrating them
Decide MFA, device trust, and provisioning source-of-truth approach

phases.name: Build and mirror
activities: Stand up target IdP, directory sync, and policies
Configure break-glass and logging to SIEM
Mirror group structure and test with IT pilot

phases.name: Migrate in waves
activities: Run waves in the order generated
Hold a go/no-go before each wave

phases.name: Converge and retire
activities: Remove old SSO trust and secrets per app
Archive logs and update runbooks and audit evidence

cutover_checklist: Go/no-go signed by wave owner and security
Pilot users confirmed working on the target before broad switch
App vendor contacted where IdP swap needs vendor action
Helpdesk briefed with a one-page FAQ and escalation path
Break-glass admin login verified outside the new IdP
Old IdP configuration exported and saved before any change
Monitoring on sign-in failure rate with an agreed rollback threshold
rollback: Per app: restore previous IdP metadata and certificate (kept from the pre-change export)
Per app: re-enable old provisioning only after disabling the new connector
Domain federation: documented revert command and who may run it
Rollback trigger: sign-in failure rate or helpdesk ticket threshold agreed in advance
exit_criteria: Zero sign-ins to the old IdP for 30 days except break-glass
All provisioning owned by a single system
MFA enrollment at target percentage with recovery tested
Audit evidence reviewed by the security/compliance owner
